summary.headline: D. B. Corp Q2 FY27 consolidated revenue fell to INR614 crore (from INR635 crore) and PAT to INR69 crore (from INR93 crore), largely on a festive shift into Q3.
summary.overview: Consolidated Q2 FY27 total revenue was INR614 crore versus INR635 crore a year earlier, with EBITDA up to INR124 crore from INR115 crore and PAT down to INR69 crore from INR93 crore. Management attributes the advertising decline (INR411 crore vs INR439 crore) mainly to about 8 days of Navratri moving from Q2 into Q3, which it sizes at roughly INR40 crore; excluding this shift, advertising and EBITDA grew at a positive single-digit rate. Newsprint cost per tonne rose about 21% year on year, and management expects only a 2-3% softening in Q3 and Q4. Radio revenue and EBITDA both declined in Q2, while H1 radio EBITDA improved.

segments.name: Radio
segments.commentary: Q2 FY27 revenue INR39 crore (vs INR43 crore) and EBITDA INR11 crore (vs INR13 crore). H1 FY27 revenue stable at INR82 crore, with EBITDA up to INR26 crore from INR24 crore.

segments.name: Print (advertising and circulation)
segments.commentary: Advertising INR411 crore (down from INR439 crore) on festive timing; circulation INR116 crore (down from INR121 crore) with about 37.68 lakh copies, roughly flat quarter on quarter but about 30,000 copies lower.

segments.name: Digital
segments.commentary: No revenue disclosed. Monthly active users reportedly fell from 20 million in Q4 to 18 million; marketing spend was cut and an app subscription price test moved from INR149 to INR199 on an experimental basis.

guidance_outlook: Management is aiming for high single-digit to early double-digit full-year advertising revenue growth, described as an endeavour rather than a firm guidance.
Newsprint prices are expected to fall 2-3% in Q3 and Q4 per suppliers, and about 2% versus Q2 levels; year-on-year Q3 newsprint cost is still seen 18-20% higher.
No large capex is planned for the next 4-5 quarters, as machinery and production equipment are already in place.
Cash and bank balance is about INR1,120 crore; INR5 per share first interim dividend was paid in Q1, and further distribution will be decided by the Board.
No cover price hike is planned; management says a price increase would accelerate circulation decline.
capex_capacity: No major capex planned for the next 4-5 quarters because machines and production equipment are in place.
Circulation at about 38 lakh copies (37.68 lakh), flat sequentially; management is focusing on core markets and letting non-core copies decline.
Inventory held: a few months of Indian newsprint (transport 10-15 days) and about a quarter for imported paper.
demand_pricing: Newsprint cost per tonne rose from about INR47,000 to about INR57,000, an increase of about 21% year on year, attributed to geopolitical factors and higher freight.
Advertising ticket size is being raised by upgrading inside-page advertisers to back, third and front pages at prevailing rates.

Sector trends: real estate single digit (festive-shift affected), jewellery strong, BFSI/IPO business up about 50% from a small base, healthcare strong double digit, FMCG about -2% in the quarter (single digit growth expected on a normalised basis), automobile flat, education single digit, government advertising down due to panchayat election code of conduct.
Cover price stays at INR5; management argues average monthly cost to consumers of INR150-170 is already high.

qa_highlights.question: What are the Q3 and full-year advertising and circulation revenue guidance?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the festive shift impacts about INR40 crore, and it is optimistic on the next two quarters but concerned about geopolitics and uneven monsoon; the full-year high single-digit to early double-digit target is an endeavour.

qa_highlights.question: Why did circulation decline and are cover price hikes planned?
qa_highlights.answer: Circulation is about 38 lakh copies, flat quarter on quarter. No cover price hike is planned because it would accelerate the decline.

qa_highlights.question: What is the newsprint cost trend and inventory policy?
qa_highlights.answer: Newsprint costs are up about 21% year on year (INR47,000 to INR57,000 per tonne), expected to fall 2-3% in Q3 and Q4. Inventory is held for a few months for Indian paper and about a quarter for imports.

qa_highlights.question: Why did other expenses rise quarter on quarter, and what is the digital subscription test?
qa_highlights.answer: Other expenses rose sequentially because of sales-driven events, where event costs and revenue are both booked. The INR149 to INR199 subscription price change is an experiment on about 1 lakh subscribers; results are described as decent and impact will be clearer in a couple of quarters.

qa_highlights.question: Why did MAUs decline and what is the digital revenue model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cut digital marketing spend and ran subscription experiments, and says MAU quarter-on-quarter decline is about 3-4%. Digital revenue is being built from advertising, subscriptions and technology tie-ups, all at a nascent stage; one senior digital hire has exited.

qa_highlights.question: Other income of around INR11 crore: what is it?
qa_highlights.answer: It is a gain of about INR13.39 crore from derecognising the right-of-use asset and lease liability after the Ahmedabad registered office lease was terminated, booked as other income under Ind AS 116 and 109.

risks_watch: Newsprint costs up about 21% YoY; margin pressure if the expected 2-3% sequential softening does not come through.
Circulation and readership flat for several quarters post-COVID; management concedes limited growth, and the advertising base depends on readership.
Digital MAUs declining (20 million to 18 million) with marketing spend cut; subscription pricing outcome still unclear.
Q3 advertising recovery depends on festive demand and geopolitical conditions; government advertising hit by election code of conduct.
Management has not disclosed digital revenue; a Board decision on providing more digital disclosure is pending.
summary.management_tone: Management was confident on the underlying business and festive outlook but defensive on the YoY decline, repeatedly attributing it to timing. It was evasive on digital metrics and on longer-term print structure, deferring to one-on-one investor relations meetings and a future Board decision.
key_quotes: So on a like -to-like basis, D. B. Corp advertising revenue and EBITDA registered positive single-digit growth in Q2 excluding the impact of this festive shift.
What we were paying INR47,000 per tonne average cost, we are paying right now almost INR57,000.

So right now, what is happening, the whole digital genre, if you look at the advertising is pretty, I would say, unclear for everybody because at one side, there's an extra inventory coming from multiple sources.
